free_tier.stated: KVM AMD Ryzen I at EUR 9.99/month (the tracker writes the euro sign; transliterated here for ASCII): 4 Ryzen cores fair-share, 2,048 MB RAM, 25 GB NVMe, 2,000 GB/month bandwidth, 1 Gbps port, 1 IPv4 + IPv6, Lelystad Netherlands. The tracker's line reads "starting at EUR 9.99 per month". The ladder above it: KVM AMD Ryzen II at EUR 14.99/month with 4 cores, 4,096 MB and 40 GB NVMe; KVM AMD Ryzen III at EUR 21.99 with 6 cores, 6,144 MB and 60 GB NVMe. The vendor's own store page for the same product confirms the shape and not the price.

egress.terms: 2 TB a month on the Ryzen I plan, stated as a plan line both by the tracker and by the vendor store page ("Bandwidth - 2TB"); the vendor runs a separate unmetered 10 Gbit and 40 Gbit dedicated line, which is a different product

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: KVM with root, sold through a WHMCS store at hostslick.com/clients, so any client runs inside the VM and no wrapper is needed; no API was documented on either page read.
chaining: 4 Ryzen cores and 2 GB for EUR 9.99 is the most CPU per euro, which fits a short build or a compile job rather than a serving node 2 TB a month caps it as a crawler front end and the 25 GB disk caps it as anything that holds data.

limits.value: 2,000 GB a month is about 66 GB a day, 6.6 percent of one day of the 1 TB serving target, and the 25 GB NVMe disk holds no working set; the 4 shared Ryzen cores are the only generous part of the plan.
